verdict.probe_answer: Both arms add tests that would fail on the pre-change code: the parse test would not compile/pass because WorkflowNodeToml had no retry field, and the graph-mapping test would observe WorkflowNode.retry as None. Both assert real behavior for the required path by using RegistryConfig::load_workflows for the mandatory mapping test. Neither arm adds meaningful negative or edge coverage beyond the requested default None for omitted backoff_cap_ms. Arm A's strongest test is workflow_node_retry_maps_into_graph because it exercises the real loader and asserts the resulting RetryPolicy; its weakest is workflow_node_retry_parses because it only verifies TOML deserialization. Arm B's strongest test is also workflow_node_retry_maps_into_graph; its weakest is workflow_node_retry_parses, slightly weaker than A's because it does not assert backoff_cap_ms is None.
verdict.rationale: Arm B is the better implementation because it completes T3 with the requested config-only changes and mandatory load_workflows mapping test while staying in scope. Arm A also completes the functional task and has marginally stronger parse-test assertion, but it edits crates/bridge-workflow/src/graph.rs even though T3 was explicitly scoped to bin/a2a-bridge/src/config.rs. That extra RetryPolicy change appears behavior-preserving, so it is not a WRONG finding, but it is an out-of-scope SMELL under the task's strict scope discipline. The difference is enough to prefer B materially despite A's tiny test-strength edge.
